newsitem.title: USA: Westinghouse posts $28 million net loss.
newsitem.headline: Westinghouse posts $28 million net loss.

text.p: Westinghouse Electric Corp. said Monday that it posted a $28 million loss in the third quarter after taking a $30 million after-tax charge related to early retirement of debt.
The company said it had a net loss of $28 million, or 6 cents a share, for the three months ended Sept. 30, compared with a net loss of $52 million, or 15 cents a share, a year earlier.
The per-share loss was far greater than Wall Street estimates of 1 cent a share, according to First Call, which tracks analysts' estimates.

Westinghouse said the loss included a $30 million after-tax charge for the write-off of financing fees related to the replacement of a $7.5 billion credit facility with $5.5 billion in revolving credit with more favourable terms.

The company, which acquired the CBS television network this year, said its revenues for the quarter expanded to $2.04 billion from $1.28 billion, with CBS helping to send broadcasting group sales soaring to $910 million from $166 million.

Westinghouse said power systems sales, which account for about two-thirds of its revenues, increased significantly during the quarter. But profits were flat due to changes in the sales mix and lower prices in equipment backlog.
The unit makes products ranging from nuclear reactors to refrigerated trucks.

The company did not have any comment on reports that it was considering separating its media businesses, which will include the soon-to-be-acquired Infinity Broadcasting Corp., from its less-profitable industrial units.
Chairman Michael H. Jordan expressed satisfaction with the integration of CBS into Westinghouse's existing Group W broadcasting group.

"CBS has increased viewership among households and has grown target demographics," he said in a statement. "This improved network performance, our increased focus on station operations and cost reduction programmes will drive stronger results at the TV stations."

Westinghouse said its net income for the first nine months of the year almost tripled to $64 million, or 14 cents a share, from $22 million, which amounted to a loss of 3 cents a share due to a 22 cents-a-share net loss on the disposal of WCI Communities Inc.
Westinghouse's stock slipped 12.5 cents to $17.375 in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
